---
title: "Plan to better implement 504/IEP accommodations in Algebra 2"
output: pdf_document
---

From Huston's emails and rereading through the 504/IEP accommodations, I understand the need for:

* Clear demarcation of reduced-load work.
    * Fewer practice problems of the same type
    * Fewer types of problems
        * Identifying problems as "must-do" and "reach"


* Currently, I often give packets with a dozen versions of the same question. I have been telling students they can get full credit without completing them all. I simply think having more opportunity to practice can be helpful.

* Simply offering fewer opportunities to practice to reduced-work students does not seem helpful. But it seems that having only vocal reminders that full credit is given for good-faith effort are insufficient. **I could state in the instructions on the page a "must do" number?**
